title: On the ancestry and evolution of the extinct dire wolf.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Zenodo record 18624787 (CC-BY-4.0) holds 3 files: supplementary tables xlsx (3.4 MB, downloaded and opened: 18 sheets, the largest are S5 with 19,281 per-gene read-depth rows and S9 with 3,950 mitochondrial sequence accessions), a variant-call TSV.gz (120.8 MB, over the 50 MB cap; I read only the header and first rows with a ranged download: chr, pos, ref, alt, genotypes/depths for 2 dire wolves DireGB and DireSP, plus SnpEff annotation columns), and a genome assembly FASTA (734.6 MB, not downloaded).
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Coverage of 3.4x and 12.8x, sample ages, and the ~2/3 vs ~1/3 ancestry split come from the abstract. Raw reads are in SRA BioProject PRJNA1222369 (raw sequencing, not touched).

a1_downloadable.note: Zenodo files download openly under CC-BY-4.0; checked in files.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: No outcome to predict. The files are genotype calls for 2 extinct individuals, per-gene coverage and phylogenetic summary tables; any ML target would have to be constructed. Checked in files.

a3_inputs_present.note: Variant positions and alleles are present in the TSV; checked header and first rows.

a4_units_stated.note: Read depth and genotype quality columns follow VCF (variant call format) conventions; no real label exists, so units don't apply.

a5_enough_rows.note: The biological unit is the individual: 2 dire wolves plus about 10 reference species. The variant row count was not counted (file over the cap), and it wouldn't matter.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~121 MB variant TSV.gz plus a 3.4 MB xlsx
a6_fits_laptop.note: Small, but there is no task to run.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: 2 samples (DireGB, DireSP) in the TSV header match the abstract's two paleogenomes (genomes recovered from ancient remains).

a8_label_provenance.note: The only label-like columns (variant impact, variant type) are SnpEff output, i.e. a rule-based annotation tool's prediction computed from the variants themselves.

honest_claim_h3: No honest ML claim is possible: with two ancient genomes there is nothing to train on and no measured outcome.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use dire wolf DNA variants to predict which genes changed in function, a project with no measured answers to learn from.
plain_idea.train_on: Genotype calls at variant sites for 2 extinct dire wolves (row count unknown; the 121 MB file was only partly read).
plain_idea.predict: Variant functional impact, but the only available 'answers' are SnpEff annotations, which are rule-based predictions and not measurements.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: It isn't, as an ML project: this is an evolutionary-history paper whose value is in the phylogeny (the family tree) and admixture (mixing of lineages), not in a learnable dataset.

ml_idea: None viable. Two ancient genomes with no measured outcome; the variant table is useful as a reference resource for canid population genetics, not as ML training data.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated; there is no task to build.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the individuals (2) and look for a measured outcome column (none). Done.

verdict_reason: Fails A2, A5 and A8: the Zenodo files hold genotypes for only 2 ancient dire wolves plus summary tables, with no measured outcome. The only label-like columns are SnpEff annotations computed from the variants.
